newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican leader charged by magistrate.
newsitem.headline: Corsican leader charged by magistrate.

text.p: A suspected leader of the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) was placed under investigation and jailed in Paris on Saturday as a crackdown continued against separatists on the Mediterranean island.

Justice sources said Jean-Michel Rossi, a leading member of A Cuncolta Naziunalista, the political arm of the FLNC, was being investigated for suspected membership of a terrorist group and offences against weapons laws.
Rossi is editor of the stridently nationalist newspaper U Ribombu (The Thunderclap) which has itself been investigated for possible legal action over alleged threats contained in its columns.
He is the third leading member of A Cuncolta detained in the past few weeks in a crackdown stepped up after FLNC guerrillas bombed the mayoral office of Prime Minister Alain Juppe in Bordeaux.
The head of A Cuncolta, Francois Santoni, and his lawyer girlfriend, Marie-Helene Mattei, have been held since last month.
Rossi, who had been in hiding for weeks, gave himself up on Tuesday after police arrested some 15 members or sympathisers of Conculta in raids in Corsica and southern France.
Six suspected separatist militants who were flown to Paris after being arrested in Corsica during the week were placed under investigation on Friday in the same case as that of Rossi.
They are suspected of involvement in the machine-gunning of a hotel in the town of Aregno in October, the sources said. The FLNC has claimed responsibility for the attack.

The legal moves took place after police discovered an explosive charge made up of three sticks of dynamite which failed to go off after being placed overnight outside a bank in the central Corsican town of Sartene.
There was no indication of who was responsible but separatists were suspected.
